{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "l0rinc",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK"
    },
    {
      "login": "ajtowns",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; asked about behavior on already-pruned nodes and suggested -prunetxindex option"
    },
    {
      "login": "mzumsande",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "suggested partial indexing on already-pruned nodes (implemented)"
    },
    {
      "login": "arejula27",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "Concept ACK; suggested returning structured block hashes, prune policy enum, std::variant lookup results, and additional tests"
    },
    {
      "login": "fjahr",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "objected to getindexinfo synced: true semantic change; suggested splitting plain prune mode from partial indexing"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:5405875239",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "What is the intended behavior when txindex is enabled on an already pruned node?",
      "quote": "What's the (intended) behaviour if you enable txindex on a node that is already pruned?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author explained it triggers the same startup error as coinstatsindex or blockfilterindex",
      "author_replies": ["c:5464600208"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:5464600208",
      "status_by_quote": "It's the same behavior if you try and start coinstatsindex or blockfilterindex after you've pruned past their last indexed block"
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5133416418",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Consider a partial index that only indexes non-pruned data so txindex can be enabled on already-pruned nodes",
      "quote": "However, it would have the big upside that it could be enabled on an already pruned node.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author updated the PR to support partial indexing on already-pruned nodes",
      "author_replies": ["c:5572809511", "c:5593930757"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5593930757",
      "status_by_quote": "I've updated this change to also allow starting an index with an already pruned node."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5190953631",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Return pruned block hashes as structured data rather than inside the error string",
      "quote": "Right now those hashes only reach the caller inside the error string, so automating the fetch and retry means parsing the message. Would returning them as structured data be worth it?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author returned pruned block hashes in optional data field of JSON error response",
      "author_replies": ["c:5724803370"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5724803370",
      "status_by_quote": "I added returning the pruned block hashes in an optional data field of the JSON error response."
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5190953631",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Use a single enum rather than two separate flags in BaseIndex to express prune policy invariants",
      "quote": "Would a single enum value express that relationship better, so the invariant lives in the type instead of a convention that a future index could break?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author replaced AllowPrune with GetPrunePolicy returning an enum",
      "author_replies": ["c:5724803370"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:5724803370",
      "status_by_quote": "I renamed AllowPrune to GetPrunePolicy which returns an enum."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4092299815",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Use std::variant<TxFound, TxMiss> rather than one struct to ensure consistent fields",
      "quote": "My proposal is to use `std::variant<TxFound, TxMiss>` rather than one struct where the outcome is implied by which fields are set.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4092330475",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Add test coverage for pruned blocks outside active chain and returning multiple candidate pruned block hashes",
      "quote": "I would add two more scenarios, as I have tested them and they are not covered",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4092377528",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "style",
      "text": "Whether result can be returned directly instead of reconstructing the object",
      "quote": "Is there a reason not to `return result;` directly?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4092387238",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Use a neutral base error message like 'Transaction not found' when appending partial history details in gettxoutproof",
      "quote": "Maybe use a neutral base message here too when the partial history detail is appended, e.g. \"Transaction not found\"?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5302843066",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Report the pruned block hash in gettxoutproof when the transaction has unspent outputs",
      "quote": "Would it make sense to report that hash too?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5302843066",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Mention deleting the index directory to rebuild partial history from disk when an index falls behind pruned data",
      "quote": "Would it be worth mentioning that for indexes that allow partial history?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4121208795",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Changing the semantics of synced: true in getindexinfo may break clients that do not check first_block_height",
      "quote": "`synced: true` doesn't really mean the same thing as before. So some clients which are not checking the new `first_block_height` may not get what they think they are getting.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4121237318",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Consider requiring an explicit opt-in flag for partial indexing to communicate the behavior clearly to users",
      "quote": "Starting with `-prune=XXX -txindex=1` may give you a partial or full txindex depending on if you had the index on before. Possibly the partial index could use an explicit opt-in?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4121354564",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Whether all information in TxIndexMissErrorDetails like the synced check can ever be hit given f_txindex_ready",
      "quote": "Because of what we do with `f_txindex_ready` above I am not sure all the infos in `TxIndexMissErrorDetails` would ever be relevant or possible to hit",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5337393375",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "Split the PR into enabling plain prune mode first and keep partial indexing for a follow-up",
      "quote": "Would you mind splitting the PR into enabling plain prune mode and keep the partial index and all the related refactorings for a follow-up to that?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "c:5321848392",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "Big concept ACK \\:D/",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5405875239",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "I think expected block usage is about 100GB per year, so 5 years worth of history would be half a terabyte, and probably cover most lookups... Concept ACK, looks okay to me at first glance.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5190953631",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "I'm excited about this PR and I love the idea and the approach... we can even access txs on pruned nodes, since #35531 the index stores the block 'virtual' reference rather than a file position",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "respond to review comments and suggestions from arejula27 and fjahr, including fjahr's suggestion to split the PR",
      "id": "r:5337393375"
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Brought record up to date with new schema: converted mzumsande's and arejula27's earlier items to suggestions, added ajtowns' question and arejula27's prune policy enum suggestion, and recorded fjahr's review comments, including an objection on getindexinfo synced semantics and a suggestion to split the PR."
}

claims.text: Return pruned block hashes as structured data rather than inside the error string
claims.quote: Right now those hashes only reach the caller inside the error string, so automating the fetch and retry means parsing the message. Would returning them as structured data be worth it?
claims.status_note: author returned pruned block hashes in optional data field of JSON error response
claims.status_by_quote: I added returning the pruned block hashes in an optional data field of the JSON error response.

claims.text: Use a single enum rather than two separate flags in BaseIndex to express prune policy invariants
claims.quote: Would a single enum value express that relationship better, so the invariant lives in the type instead of a convention that a future index could break?
claims.status_note: author replaced AllowPrune with GetPrunePolicy returning an enum
claims.status_by_quote: I renamed AllowPrune to GetPrunePolicy which returns an enum.

claims.text: Use std::variant<TxFound, TxMiss> rather than one struct to ensure consistent fields
claims.quote: My proposal is to use `std::variant<TxFound, TxMiss>` rather than one struct where the outcome is implied by which fields are set.

claims.text: Add test coverage for pruned blocks outside active chain and returning multiple candidate pruned block hashes
claims.quote: I would add two more scenarios, as I have tested them and they are not covered

claims.text: Whether result can be returned directly instead of reconstructing the object
claims.quote: Is there a reason not to `return result;` directly?

claims.text: Use a neutral base error message like 'Transaction not found' when appending partial history details in gettxoutproof
claims.quote: Maybe use a neutral base message here too when the partial history detail is appended, e.g. "Transaction not found"?

claims.text: Report the pruned block hash in gettxoutproof when the transaction has unspent outputs
claims.quote: Would it make sense to report that hash too?

claims.text: Mention deleting the index directory to rebuild partial history from disk when an index falls behind pruned data
claims.quote: Would it be worth mentioning that for indexes that allow partial history?

claims.text: Changing the semantics of synced: true in getindexinfo may break clients that do not check first_block_height
claims.quote: `synced: true` doesn't really mean the same thing as before. So some clients which are not checking the new `first_block_height` may not get what they think they are getting.

claims.text: Consider requiring an explicit opt-in flag for partial indexing to communicate the behavior clearly to users
claims.quote: Starting with `-prune=XXX -txindex=1` may give you a partial or full txindex depending on if you had the index on before. Possibly the partial index could use an explicit opt-in?

claims.text: Whether all information in TxIndexMissErrorDetails like the synced check can ever be hit given f_txindex_ready
claims.quote: Because of what we do with `f_txindex_ready` above I am not sure all the infos in `TxIndexMissErrorDetails` would ever be relevant or possible to hit

claims.text: Split the PR into enabling plain prune mode first and keep partial indexing for a follow-up
claims.quote: Would you mind splitting the PR into enabling plain prune mode and keep the partial index and all the related refactorings for a follow-up to that?

claims.text: add a -prunetxindex=1 option to allow looking up txs without extra disk growth
claims.quote: I'd definitely prefer to have a -prunetxindex=1 option I could set, so that my prune=2000 (~1 week worth of blocks) node could lookup txs without needing to be reprovisioned with extra disk though.
claims.status_note: author replied this could be added as a follow-up
claims.status_by_quote: I think that could be added as a follow-up, and would not conflict with this approach.

support.reason: I think expected block usage is about 100GB per year, so 5 years worth of history would be half a terabyte, and probably cover most lookups... Concept ACK, looks okay to me at first glance.
I'm excited about this PR and I love the idea and the approach... we can even access txs on pruned nodes, since #35531 the index stores the block 'virtual' reference rather than a file position
